findings.concern: parsePushPayload's doc comment explicitly claims 'every field is typeof-checked, not merely nullish-checked ... a bare ?? would let it through unchanged' as the module's stated defensive-against-attacker-influenced-network-input design rule. In fact only title, body and data.route receive a typeof === 'string' guard; icon, badge, tag and actions are only a nullish (undefined) check and then passed through unchecked, despite the inline cast typing them as string. A malformed payload such as {icon: 12345} or {actions: "x"} flows through unchanged into ResolvedPushNotificationOptions and then into showNotification's options with the wrong runtime type. This is both a comment/code mismatch and a real (if narrow) robustness gap against the module's own stated threat model. Confirmed independently and by the dispatched code-reviewer-semantic sub-agent.

NotificationsCard has no onUnauthorized prop (its only prop is {canWrite: boolean}) and none of its authenticated-API-calling paths (load/performSubscribe/handleUnsubscribe/handleSendTest, all of which call fetchVapidPublicKey/subscribeToPush/unsubscribeFromPush/sendTestPush) check for a 401 to route to re-authentication -- every caught error instead falls into a generic pt-BR 'tente novamente' message. This is inconsistent with (a) the plan's own cited Mirror source GoogleConnectionCard.tsx, whose load() checks cause.status === 401 and calls onUnauthorized, and (b) this same diff's own sibling screen NotificationsDiagnosticsScreen.tsx, which implements that exact branch. NotificationsScreen.tsx receives onUnauthorized as a prop (per Task 11's stated prop list) but never uses it (destructured as _onUnauthorized) and never threads it into NotificationsCard. Net effect: a bearer-token expiry while on the Notificacoes screen leaves the owner stuck in a generic failure state on every write action, with no route back to the token gate, unlike the rest of the app's established 401 convention. Confirmed independently and by the dispatched code-reviewer-semantic sub-agent.
